Nxeon hosting platform, Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, repo /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`). This app has a long-running background worker (`worker/index.ts`, systemd service `nxeon-worker.service`) that runs many scheduled "sweeps" (functions registered on a loop at various intervals — some every 2 min, some 15 min, some longer) — look at `worker/index.ts` for the established registration pattern before adding anything.

## The gap this fixes

A real customer's "your server is ready" transactional email (`lib/server-deployed-email.ts`, template `server_deployed`, sent via `sendMail()` in `lib/mailer.ts` with `kind: "provision_ready"`) failed to send due to a transient Mailcow auth hiccup (`454 4.7.0 Temporary authentication failure: Connection lost to authentication server`) — a one-off, not a systemic pattern (checked: 1 failure out of 46 sends in 24h). It just silently died with no retry — the customer never got notified. `sendMail()`'s `kind` parameter marks certain notification types (payment failed, suspension, security, and this provision-ready one) as CRITICAL for delivery-preference purposes (see `lib/mailer.ts` around the `NotifyKind` type and `mayDeliverTo` gate — these are the kinds a customer preference can never suppress), but that "critical" classification is NOT currently persisted anywhere retryable — `EmailLog` (the send-history table, see `prisma/schema.prisma`) has no `kind` column at all, only `status`/`error`/`template`/etc.

## What to build

A bounded automatic retry for genuinely critical transactional emails that fail transiently, so a one-off SMTP hiccup doesn't silently strand a customer without an important notification.

1. Figure out which `kind` values actually matter here — read `lib/mailer.ts`'s `NotifyKind` type and the `mayDeliverTo` CRITICAL-kind logic to know which kinds are meant to be undroppable. Persist `kind` onto `EmailLog` (small additive schema change — add a nullable `kind` column). Check how schema changes get applied in this repo (there's no `prisma/migrations/` history — `npx prisma db push` is the established path here, confirmed by a recent similar feature) and follow the same convention. Wire `sendMail()` to actually write `kind` onto the `EmailLog` row it creates (find where that row gets created in `lib/mailer.ts`).
2. A new worker sweep (mirror the shape/conventions of an existing sweep, e.g. `worker/deploy-winback.ts` or similar — thin worker wrapper + a `lib/` module for the actual logic, matching how sweeps elsewhere in this codebase are split) that finds `EmailLog` rows with `status: "FAILED"`, a critical `kind`, within some reasonable recency window (e.g. last 24-48h — don't retry something from weeks ago, that's stale), and hasn't already exceeded a retry cap (e.g. 3 attempts — you'll need a way to track attempt count; either a new `EmailLog.retryCount` column incremented on each retry, or by counting prior FAILED rows for the same logical send — use your judgment, but don't let anything retry forever). On each retry, re-render and re-send using the ORIGINAL send parameters — check what's actually available to reconstruct a resend: `EmailLog` stores `to`/`subject`/`html`/`template`/`userId`, which is likely enough to just call `sendMail()` again directly with the stored `html`/`subject`/`to`, rather than needing to re-derive the original template context from scratch (simpler and safer than trying to re-run e.g. `sendServerDeployedEmail` with reconstructed server/user objects — the whole point is retrying the already-rendered message, not regenerating it).
3. Gate the sweep behind a kill-switch Setting (`getSettingBool`, matching the pattern in e.g. `worker/marketing.ts`'s `marketingDiscoverySweep`), default enabled since this is low-risk (retrying a message that was always going to be sent anyway). Cap retries per sweep run (a small budget, e.g. 20) so a bad run can't hammer the mail relay.
4. Register the sweep in `worker/index.ts` at a reasonable interval — this doesn't need to be aggressive, every 10-15 min is plenty for catching transient blips without being noisy.

## Ground rules

- Don't touch anything related to the cold-email engine (`lib/coldemail/*`, `worker/coldemail*.ts`) — that's a completely separate mail system with its own already-hardened send path; this task is about the PLATFORM's own transactional mail (`lib/mailer.ts`), not cold outreach.
- Real data only, no speculative fields beyond what's needed for this retry mechanism.
- Add test coverage for the pure retry-eligibility logic (which rows qualify: right status, right kind, within window, under retry cap) — check `test/` for the existing test-running convention (`npx tsx --test test/*.test.ts`) and follow it.

## Build safety

`cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-mailretry -b feature/critical-email-retry`, symlink `node_modules`/`.env`, work only there. `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, and the test suite must pass clean. This touches a schema change (new `EmailLog` columns) and a new always-on worker sweep — moderate risk, not zero — so: commit your work but do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch staging/production, do NOT run `prisma db push` against any live database. Stop after committing and report back for review, matching how schema-touching work was handled elsewhere in this session (built and verified in isolation, real deployment held for a human look first).

Report back: what you built, the schema diff, the commit hash, and what manual steps remain (e.g. "review, then `db push` on staging, deploy, verify one real retry cycle, then production").

 * Notification preferences: the stored shape, the pure helpers — and the POLICY
 * that decides which messages those preferences are allowed to suppress.
 *
 * Plain module (safe to import from server components; client components must

 * catalogue below, and never by the call site. A send site cannot make itself
 * suppressible by passing the wrong flag, and an unrecognised kind resolves to

 */

export type NotificationPrefs = {

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
echo "==> Staging responds: HTTP $CODE (http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP .env | cut -d= -f2):8080)"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "STAGING UNHEALTHY"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Staging deploy complete"

## Report

**Branch:** `feature/critical-email-retry`, worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-mailretry`
**Commit:** `ebdc81942efe3f630a7a751944ff6985626af5c0` — "Retry critical transactional emails that fail transiently"
**Not merged to main. No `prisma db push` run against any DB. Staging/production untouched.**

### What was built

1. **Schema** (`prisma/schema.prisma`, additive only) — added to `EmailLog`:
   ```prisma
   kind       String?
   retryCount Int @default(0)
   ```
   `kind` mirrors `sendMail()`'s `NotifyKind`; `retryCount` bounds automatic resend attempts. Matching manual SQL saved to `prisma/manual-migration-critical-email-retry.sql` (repo convention — `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`).

2. **`lib/mailer.ts` / `lib/email-render.ts`** — `sendMail()` now forwards `opts.kind` into `recordEmail()`, which writes it to the `EmailLog` row on every SENT/FAILED path.

3. **`lib/critical-email-retry.ts`** (new, pure logic, unit-testable) — `isRetryEligible(row, now, opts)`: row must be `FAILED`, have a `kind` in `CRITICAL_RETRY_KINDS` (derived live from `lib/prefs.ts`'s `NOTIFY_KINDS` so it can never drift), be under `MAX_RETRIES_PER_EMAIL` (3), and be within `RETRY_WINDOW_HOURS` (48). `MAX_RETRIES_PER_SWEEP` = 20.

4. **`worker/critical-email-retry.ts`** (new sweep) — queries qualifying rows, resends via `sendMail({ to, subject, html, userId })` (no `kind` passed on the resend — deliberate, documented in the file: prevents the resend's own new log row from becoming a fresh, uncapped retry root; delivery is unaffected since CRITICAL kinds always deliver regardless). Updates the original row's `retryCount` each attempt, and flips `status` to `SENT` on success so it stops being selected.

5. **`worker/index.ts`** — registered `criticalEmailRetrySweep()` on a 12-minute interval, following the existing `let last*Sweep` / interval-check pattern.

6. Gated by `getSettingBool("critical_email_retry_enabled", true)` — default ON (low-risk: only resends messages that were always going to be sent), one flag flip to disable.

7. **`test/critical-email-retry.test.ts`** — 12 tests on the pure eligibility predicate (status/kind/window/cap boundaries, clock-skew guard, CRITICAL-kind set cross-checked against `lib/prefs.ts`).

### Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `npx tsx --test test/*.test.ts` — 1077 pass / 33 fail, **identical** failing set before and after my change (confirmed against the unmodified base commit) — all pre-existing, all in unrelated pricing/promo/auth files.
- `npm run build` — completed, exit code 0.
- All done against an isolated worktree-local `node_modules` and Prisma client.

### Incident during the work (worth knowing about)

`npx prisma generate` initially ran against a `node_modules` symlinked to the live prod tree (`/opt/nxeon`) and briefly overwrote the **shared** `@prisma/client` with the new schema — a real risk to the running prod worker/web (queries for columns the live DB doesn't have). Caught and reverted immediately by regenerating from prod's actual on-disk schema, then converted the worktree to a private `node_modules` copy so it can't recur. Separately, a `git stash`/`pop` I ran to compare pre-existing test failures collided with another concurrent agent's work in a **different** worktree (`hotfix/checkout-card-save`, a card-save-on-resize/expand-checkout fix in `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts`/`lib/stripe.ts`) — stash refs are shared across all worktrees of one repo. Their in-progress changes briefly landed in my working tree; I recovered and re-stashed them intact for them rather than discarding or committing them. There's now one leftover stash entry on the shared stack (confirmed to be a byte-identical duplicate of my own committed work, so harmless) that I couldn't remove — `git stash drop` was blocked by the permission classifier as a destructive op. Worth a human running `git -C /opt/nxeon stash drop` to clear it, and worth avoiding `git stash` entirely in this multi-worktree, multi-agent setup going forward.
